problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=3t,\,y=\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2},\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}t & =\frac{x}{3},\,{t}^{2}=\frac{2}{3}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=\frac{2}{3}y$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9} & =\frac{2}{3}y \\ {x}^{2} & =6y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian equation of the parabola is ${x}^{2}=6y.$
